samples.summary: Revalidation only tightens authority for docs/sheets/board; slides and notes still capture `readOnly` once, so an editor→viewer downgrade never reaches them
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` now re-resolves the token every 60s and pushes the fresh `role` down (`shared-document.tsx:1089-1120`), and each layout derives `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (`shared-document.tsx:330, 383, 433, 460`). Only `docs-view.tsx` (this delta), `board-view.tsx:851` and `sheet-view.tsx:1341` list `readOnly` in the mount-effect deps. `slides-view.tsx:1222-1228` explicitly excludes it — "it is derived from a share-link role that is fixed for the lifetime of the route, so toggling it at runtime is not a supported scenario" — and `notes-view.tsx:157` also mounts on `[didMount, doc]` only. This delta invalidates exactly that assumption without updating either view, so on a slides or notes share link a downgraded visitor keeps a fully writable editor, and with the default `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset (docs/design/sharing.md:200-219) the client gate is the real write boundary. The stated outcome — bounding how long a downgraded link keeps its authority — is therefore met for only part of the shared surface, and the now-false comment in slides-view will mislead the next reader.
searchedFor: grep readOnly in slides-view.tsx, notes-view.tsx, board-view.tsx, sheet-view.tsx

samples.summary: `docs/design/sharing.md` still documents the share view as resolving the token once; the new revalidation loop and failure-eviction policy are recorded only in code comments
samples.evidence: The Frontend section ("Shared document route (`/shared/:token`) — ... Resolves the token, sets up `YorkieProvider`...", sharing.md:140-149) and the Security section's "Revocation — Deleting a ShareLink immediately invalidates the token" (line 198) describe a one-shot resolve. This delta introduces a real behavioral contract — 60s polling plus refetch-on-focus, `retry: 1`, and closing an open session to "Link unavailable" after two consecutive failures, plus rebuilding the docs editor on a mid-session role change — which is the canonical place readers look for share-link semantics. Per CONTRIBUTING.md the canonical subsystem doc should absorb this rather than leaving the rationale in a comment block in `shared-document.tsx`.
searchedFor: glob docs/design/**/*.md for a share-link doc (share-link-analytics.md, sharing.md)

samples.summary: Template gallery previews inherit the 60s resolve poll they have no need for
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` is also mounted by `template-landing.tsx:174` and `template-review-queue.tsx:136` for embedded previews of published templates. Those tokens are gallery-owned and are not expected to be downgraded mid-view, so the new interval adds a background request per open preview for no benefit. Harmless (cheap unauthenticated lookup) but the revalidation was motivated by the `/shared/:token` visitor case only; a prop or option to opt out would keep the mechanism where it is needed.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the tree. SharedDocumentByToken re-resolves the share link on an interval and on window focus (shared-document.tsx:1106-1118), and each shared layout derives readOnly from the live resolved.role (lines 330, 383, 433, 460) with no key on the DocumentProviders (1010-1075), so a role downgrade re-renders rather than remounts. docs-view.tsx:583-590 and board-view.tsx:851 list readOnly in their mount-effect deps — docs-view's comment even names SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS — while slides-view.tsx:1222-1228 keeps [didMount, doc] with an explicitly now-false justification ("fixed for the lifetime of the route"), and notes-view.tsx:127-157 keeps [didMount, doc] around initialize(container, store, theme, readOnly, ...). readOnlyMount is what feeds initializeEditor/mountThumbnailPanel/mountNotesPanel (slides-view.tsx:722, 1074, 1077). Since the auth webhook defaults to shadow mode (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101; self-hosting.md:185), the client mount is the effective write boundary, so a downgraded slides or notes visitor keeps a writable editor while only the toolbar (gated at shared-document.tsx:367/529) disappears. The change's stated outcome is thus met for only part of the shared surface — an unmet acceptance criterion with user-visible cost, not mere tidiness — and no guard elsewhere makes it unreachable.
